name: Files changed renders the reviewer-ordered diff on seeded data
description: Walks L03b on the seeded PR #482: from the PR list into the detail route, onto the Files changed tab, and over every region of the grouped diff. Like flow 11 this makes NO model call — and here that is the feature rather than a constraint on the test. Smart Diff is deterministic by construction: `GET /pulls/:id/smart-diff` classifies paths with regexes, reads `finding_lines` off the reviews already in the database, and quotes its per-file summary out of the stored patch. `server/test/smart-diff.it.test.ts` proves the recorded-calls half (every provider mock stays empty and the `jobs` table does not grow); what this flow adds is that the whole thing really reaches a browser. Four assertions carry more than their length. 'Core logic' appearing BEFORE 'Boilerplate' is the acceptance criterion — the server returns the groups in that order and the client re-imposes it from its own `GROUP_ORDER`, so a regression in either shows here. The quoted summary 'bucketKey, rateLimit' is the no-LLM claim made visible: those two identifiers were copied out of the `@@` header tails of `src/middleware/ratelimit.ts`'s patch by a pure function, and a model that invented them would say something more fluent. '1 finding' plus 'blocker' is the overlay working end to end across the join that is easiest to get quietly wrong — the seeded review carries `agent_id: null`, so a per-agent reduction keyed on the raw value would collapse it and this badge would simply not exist (see `latestFindingsPerAgent`). And `order=original` in the URL proves the toggle is real state a link can carry, not local component state. The last four steps are the point of the badges, and were added after review: a findings badge does not move the reader inside the file, it LEAVES for that finding's card in the Agent runs tab, through the app's own router. `src/api/users.ts` is chosen over `src/config.ts` deliberately — its WARNING sorts SECOND in the panel and `FindingsPanel` expands only the first card by default, so 'Loop issues one query per user' being on screen proves the target was carried through the URL rather than merely that the tab switched. What this flow still cannot assert is the scroll itself (agent-browser has no scroll-position locator); that is pinned in `FindingCard.test.tsx` ('scrolls into view when it is the finding the screen was navigated to'), along with the once-only guard that stops an accept or a refetch yanking the page back. Also not asserted: that `package-lock.json` starts COLLAPSED. The row is asserted present, but 'its patch text is absent' is a negative and this harness has only positive locators — that pin is `SmartDiffViewer.test.tsx`'s 'keeps the lock file collapsed'. Nor is the split-suggestion banner: the seeded PR is 47 changed lines against a 400-line threshold, so it correctly does not fire, and `server/test/smart-diff-split.test.ts` covers the case where it does. Precondition: a freshly-seeded DB where acme/payments-api PR #482 is the first repo — run via `npm run e2e:hermetic`. NOTE the seed changed in L03b: `SEED_PR_PATCHES` carries real unified-diff text for nine files and the PR row's totals are DERIVED from it, so the summary line reads '9 files · +47'. A database seeded before that has four patch-less rows and this flow will fail on the summary and on every code line. LOCATOR CASING: 'REVIEWER-ORDERED DIFF' is asserted in the RENDERED casing — `SectionLabel` applies `text-transform: uppercase`, so the catalogue's sentence-case 'Reviewer-ordered diff' would time out against a screen that is on and correct. The group labels are NOT uppercased (they are a plain 650-weight span), so those are asserted as written.
